root_cause.text: The `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` function casts and dereferences user-supplied payload pointers without validating that the payload buffer is large enough to contain the expected data structure, allowing out-of-bounds memory reads when undersized payloads are provided.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an `in_size` parameter and performs explicit size validation checks before dereferencing the payload. For `CXL_MBOX_OP_SET_PARTITION_INFO`, it checks `if (in_size < sizeof(*pi)) return false;` before accessing the structure. For `CXL_MBOX_OP_CLEAR_LOG`, it checks `if (in_size < sizeof(uuid_t)) return false;` before the `uuid_equal()` call. The KASAN splat shows `memcmp+0x176/0x1d0` reading 8 bytes at an out-of-bounds address during `uuid_equal()`, which occurs because a 1-byte payload was cast to a 16-byte UUID pointer and dereferenced without size validation.

intent_record.what: Added a documentation comment line describing the @in_size parameter to the cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() function's kernel-doc comment block.

It enables developers and documentation tools to understand that this parameter represents the size of the payload_in buffer in bytes, reducing ambiguity when reading the code or generated documentation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add input size validation to prevent buffer over-read when accessing user-provided payload structures.
intent_record.what: Added a new parameter `size_t in_size` to the function `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` and inserted a bounds check that validates `in_size >= sizeof(*pi)` before dereferencing the `payload_in` pointer in the `CXL_MBOX_OP_SET_PARTITION_INFO` case.
intent_record.how: The function now receives the size of the input payload and performs a runtime validation to ensure the buffer is large enough to safely contain a `cxl_mbox_set_partition_info` structure before accessing its fields. This prevents potential buffer over-read or out-of-bounds access when the caller provides an undersized payload.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add input size validation to prevent out-of-bounds memory access when casting payload_in to uuid_t in the CLEAR_LOG mailbox operation.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check in the CXL_MBOX_OP_CLEAR_LOG case that validates the input payload size is at least sizeof(uuid_t) before dereferencing the payload_in pointer as a uuid_t.
intent_record.how: This prevents out-of-bounds memory access by ensuring the input buffer is large enough to contain a complete uuid_t structure before it is cast and used. If the input size is insufficient, the function returns false early, rejecting the operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing size parameter to payload validation function call to enable proper bounds checking of user-provided input payloads.
intent_record.what: Modified the function call to `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` to pass an additional third argument `in_size` on a new line, changing from a two-argument call to a three-argument call with adjusted line wrapping.
intent_record.how: The function now receives the input payload size (`in_size`) as an additional parameter, enabling the validation logic to perform size-aware checks on user-provided payloads. This allows the function to validate not just the opcode and payload content, but also ensure the payload size is within acceptable bounds.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 6179045ccc0c6229dc449afc1701dc7fbd40571f
Author: Alison Schofield <alison.schofield@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 30 18:27:18 2022 -0700

    cxl/mbox: Block immediate mode in SET_PARTITION_INFO command
    
    User space may send the SET_PARTITION_INFO mailbox command using
    the IOCTL interface. Inspect the input payload and fail if the
    immediate flag is set.
    
    This is the first instance of the driver inspecting an input payload
    from user space. Assume there will be more
bic_trace_step.reason: The function casts the user-supplied payload_in pointer directly to 'struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info *pi' on line 243 without validating that the payload buffer is large enough to contain this structure. Line 245 then dereferences 'pi->flags' to access the flags field. If a user provides a payload smaller than sizeof(struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info), this dereference will read out-of-bounds memory. The vulnerable construct (unsafe cast and dereference of user-supplied pointer without size validation) is present and the fix is not applied in this code.
